preconditions.expression: all(c in {'b', 'w'} for c in stdin.strip())
preconditions.description: The input string consists exclusively of the characters 'b' (black) and 'w' (white).
The length of the input string is between 1 and 100,000 (inclusive).

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the maximum possible length of a contiguous alternating-color subsequence ('zebra') achievable after any number of split-reverse operations.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == max(max_alternating_subsequence(s) for s in all_possible_sequences(stdin.strip()))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum length of a contiguous alternating subsequence ('zebra') across all possible sequences obtainable by applying any number of split-reverse operations to the input string. A subsequence is alternating if no two adjacent elements are the same.
